newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Defiance says bid undervalues shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Defiance says bid undervalues shares.

text.p: Flour and bakery group Defiance Mills Ltd said on Tuesday the A$1.70 per share takeover offer by Latin American-based food and industrial giant Bunge Corp does not reflect the value of the Australian company.
"The price in my opinion does not reflect the real value of the company," Defiance chairman Tom O'Brien told Reuters.
"It does not allow for the turnaround in the performance in the company and also the improvement in the industry generally," O'Brien said.
"But the DML (Defiance) board will give it consideration and we haven't received the Part A statement yet," he said.
"I can't speak for the board, but I would be surprised if there is any real enthusiasm for an offer at that level," O'Brien said.

O'Brien did not rule out a counter-offer from Defiance for Bunge's Australian milling operations. "There is no doubt the combination of Defiance and Bunge is something that we have wanted for a long period of time."
"I would preferably like to see it another way and that is Defiance take over Bunge rather than this move," O'Brien said.
Asked if Defiance had the funds to make an offer for Bunge O'Brien repiled: "We are quickly heading in that direction."

O'Brien said he did not expect any Defiance-Bunge merger to received a knockback by anti-monopolies body, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC), because the two companies only compete in a small part of Victoria.
O'Brien said the O'Brien family controls about 40 percent of Defiance Mills issued capital. He added there were about 84 members of the O'Brien family, who have a shareholding in the miller.
Bunge said it would also offer A$2.10 per share cash for the Australian preference shares in Defiance and NZ$2.07 cash per share for New Zealand preference shares.
Defiance is dominant in the Queensland flour market and has mills in Sydney, Melbourne, Perth, Tasmania and New Zealand.
The offer was made after Tuesday's market close.
Defiance shares closed five cents lower at A$1.60.

Bunge said the aggregate value of A$97 million for the varying classes of stock represented a multiple of 20.6 times on the net income earned by Defiance in calendar 1996 and a multiple of 12.3 times earning before interest and tax.
The parent company of Bunge Australia is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and is the leading wheat miller in South America and a major global oilseed processor, it said in a statement.
Bunge Australia and major local food company Goodman Fielder Ltd abandoned a proposal to merge their Australian milling operations in May last year.
